label: original-phase input y/q/a/c (token-identity detector)
explanation: Fires mainly while the original sequence is being read (93% of mass in the original phase, never on <DEL>), when the current input is one of a small token set: y (strongest; about 40% of mass, 81% precision for y in the original phase), a, q, and more weakly c and t. The strongest activations are on y right after a or c (e.g. "a a y", "c a y"); y preceded by a/c is almost always active. Rate is highest at original positions 0-5 and falls off for later positions. Copy-phase firing is weak and rare (about 7% of mass). Almost never fires on digits, x, s, or other letters. The predicate gets most of the mass (dev mass recall 0.83) but precision is only about 0.58: q, a and c inputs often fail to fire, and which ones do depends on context that no simple history variable captures (only weakly linked to late position and earlier digits).
